topics.title: Objects, Properties & Destructuring
topics.summary: Model related data with objects, access properties safely, copy/merge records, and unpack values with destructuring.

concepts.name: Objects
concepts.explanation: Object literals group named properties. Dot notation is concise for known names; bracket notation supports computed property names.

concepts.name: Destructuring
concepts.explanation: Object and array destructuring extract values into variables and can provide defaults or rename bindings.

concepts.name: Spread
concepts.explanation: Object spread creates a shallow copy/merge. Array spread expands iterable values into a new array; neither performs a deep clone of nested objects.

topics.challenge: Create an object with at least three properties, destructure two properties, and create a modified copy using spread.
topics.hint: Destructure with const { propertyA, propertyB } = object and copy with { ...object, changed: value }.

topics.title: Array Methods & Data Transformation
topics.summary: Use map, filter, find, some, every, reduce, and sorting patterns to express collection work without manual indexing.

concepts.name: Transformation
concepts.explanation: map returns a new array with one result per input. filter returns only items that pass a predicate. Neither mutates the source array by itself.

concepts.name: Search and tests
concepts.explanation: find returns the first matching item; some asks whether any item matches; every asks whether all items match.

concepts.name: Reduction
concepts.explanation: reduce combines many values into one accumulator. Use it when the accumulator idea is genuinely clearer than a simpler loop or specialized method.

topics.challenge: Given an array of numbers, create a filtered array and a mapped array, then print both.
topics.hint: Write one callback returning a boolean for filter and one callback returning a transformed value for map.

topics.title: Forms, State & UI Rendering
topics.summary: Read form values, validate at the application layer, store UI state, and update the page from that state instead of scattering unrelated mutations.

concepts.name: Form events
concepts.explanation: submit events belong to forms. preventDefault can stop navigation when JavaScript handles the interaction locally.

concepts.name: Reading data
concepts.explanation: FormData can read successful controls by name. Input properties such as value and checked are useful for individual controls.

concepts.name: Single source of truth
concepts.explanation: Keep important UI state in a clear object, then render elements from that state. This makes behavior easier to debug than treating the DOM as hidden storage.

topics.challenge: Handle a form submit event, prevent the default submission, read at least one form value, and update text on the page.
topics.hint: Use the form submit event rather than only listening to a button click.

topics.title: Errors, Exceptions & Debugging
topics.summary: Distinguish syntax/runtime/logical errors, throw meaningful exceptions, handle recoverable failures, and debug from evidence instead of guesses.

concepts.name: Error categories
concepts.explanation: Syntax errors prevent parsing, runtime errors occur during execution, and logical errors produce the wrong result without necessarily throwing.

concepts.name: try/catch/finally
concepts.explanation: Use try/catch for failures you can meaningfully handle. finally runs cleanup code whether or not an exception occurred.

concepts.name: Debugging workflow
concepts.explanation: Read the first relevant error, inspect the stack trace, reproduce consistently, isolate inputs, and use breakpoints/watch values before changing several things at once.

topics.challenge: Write a function that throws an Error or TypeError for invalid input and handle it with try/catch.
topics.hint: Validate first, throw a meaningful exception, then catch only where you can respond usefully.

topics.title: Modules, Storage & Project Structure
topics.summary: Split code into modules with explicit imports/exports and use browser storage only for appropriate client-side state.

concepts.name: ES modules
concepts.explanation: export exposes bindings from a module; import consumes them. Module scripts have their own scope and are deferred by default in browsers.

concepts.name: Module boundaries
concepts.explanation: Group code by responsibility rather than creating one giant utility file. Public exports should form a small understandable API.

concepts.name: Web storage
concepts.explanation: localStorage stores string key/value data per origin and persists across sessions. Parse/stringify structured data and remember that storage is not a secure secret vault.

topics.challenge: Write one exported function that saves an object to localStorage and another that loads/parses it.
topics.hint: JSON.stringify before storing objects and JSON.parse after reading them back.
